doc: PyTomography's memory estimates as data. A browser (pytomo-memory.js) and Python (docs/tools/memory_model.py) evaluate this file the same way; docs/tools/check_memory_model.py proves both agree with the library.

variables: every input, with its label, unit, default, range or options. A model lists the ones it uses in 'params' and may change their defaults in 'defaults'. Booleans are true/false; options are strings; null means 'not set' (e.g. no memory budget).

derived: named expressions, evaluated in order after the parameters and settings: first the global 'derived', then each set the model names in 'use' (from 'derived_sets'), then the model's own 'derived'. Each may use the names before it.

parts: the arrays of the computation. Each part has a name ('{expr}' in it is replaced by the value), a scope ('held' for the whole run, 'subset' for one subset at a time, 'chunk' for projector or kernel temporaries), and either 'bytes' with 'on' (an expression: true puts the bytes on the GPU, false in RAM) or 'ram' and 'gpu' (bytes each). 'when' (optional) leaves the part out when false. {'include': name} inserts the parts of 'part_sets'[name]. 'repeat': {'var', 'from', 'to'} makes one part for each integer var from..to (e.g. one per bed).

combination: the peak is the sum of every part (all scopes together), plus the overheads below. GPU = sum of the GPU bytes. RAM = sum of the RAM bytes, and on Windows (gpu_counts_as_ram) the GPU bytes too.

overheads: 'fixed' (Python, PyTorch and CUDA: 3.7 GB on a CUDA device, 2.2 GB without), 'cuda_cache' (PyTorch's CUDA cache: 0.05 GB plus 20% of the GPU arrays, only if there are GPU arrays) and, on Windows, 'allocator' (memory PyTorch's allocators keep after freeing: a fraction of the RAM and GPU arrays, 0.35 by default, the model's 'allocator_fraction' if it has one).

settings: what a plan chooses, in the order it searches them (the first is the outer loop), each with its candidates fastest first. A setting is also a parameter of the same name: its present value. 'force' (optional): a value the setting always takes when not null (MLEM: one subset). 'report' (optional): the value the estimate reports and uses (e.g. lazy=null resolved). 'when' (optional): the setting exists only when true. 'type': 'bool' reports true/false.

candidates: {'items': [...], 'unique': bool, 'sort': 'asc'}; an item is {'value': expr, 'if': expr} or {'seq': {'var': k, 'from': expr, 'to': expr, 'value': expr, 'if': expr}} (k from..to inclusive; in 'if', 'value' is the item's value).

plan: every combination of the candidates in order (settings given as fixed keep their value); the first whose estimate fits both budgets (excess <= 1e-9 GB), else the one whose excess, max(0, RAM - RAM budget) + max(0, GPU - GPU budget), is least (the first of equals). On Windows the RAM budget covers the GPU memory too, since the estimate's RAM includes it.

expressions: numbers, 'strings', true, false, null, pi, names; + - * / % ** (+ also joins strings; ** is right associative; % takes the sign of the divisor), comparisons < <= > >= == != (1 or 0), && || ! (1 or 0), cond ? a : b, parentheses; functions min, max, ceil, floor, round (halves to even, as Python), abs, sqrt, log2, log10, sin, cos, asin, sig(x, n) (n significant digits, as Python's '%.ng'). All numbers are double precision.
